summary:
LUNACELL GRID is an energy-planning and optimization tool designed to support lunar south-pole mission planning. It combines NASA/JPL Horizons data on the positions of the Sun and Earth with a constrained energy optimization model to evaluate how changing illumination and communication windows affect mission power availability.

The system models solar generation, battery storage, electricity distribution, and mission energy demand to determine how available resources can be allocated more effectively. It aims to help users compare candidate landing sites and dates, assess whether proposed energy configurations can support essential operations, and identify potential improvements in storage and energy scheduling.

By making these comparisons more accessible and understandable, LUNACELL GRID addresses the challenge of translating complex astronomical data into practical mission-planning decisions. Its longer-term vision is to make lunar energy analysis more transparent, reproducible, and accessible to researchers, educators, and the wider space community.
details:
Project Details — LUNACELL GRID

LUNACELL GRID is a lunar energy-planning and optimization system designed to help evaluate the feasibility of powering missions at different lunar south-pole landing sites and dates.

How it works

The system uses NASA/JPL Horizons ephemeris data to obtain the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth relative to selected lunar locations. These observations provide time-dependent illumination and potential direct-to-Earth communication windows.

This information feeds into an electrical energy optimization model built around a simulated lunar power network. The model considers solar generation, battery charging and discharging, energy distribution between connected stations, transmission constraints, and mission electricity demand.

Using constrained linear programming, the optimizer determines how available energy should be allocated across different time intervals. It prioritizes essential electrical loads, reduces unmet energy demand, and schedules flexible mission activities around available resources. The system also explores alternative solar and battery configurations to identify improvements in mission energy feasibility.

Benefits and intended impact

LUNACELL GRID aims to bridge the gap between astronomical observations and practical electrical engineering decisions. Rather than presenting sunlight and communication windows as isolated measurements, it connects these environmental conditions to mission power requirements.

Its intended impact is to support more informed comparisons of lunar landing sites, improve energy-resource planning, and make complex mission-planning information more accessible to researchers, educators and the wider space community.

The underlying optimization framework also has potential applications in remote solar microgrids, particularly communities where limited generation and storage must be carefully allocated among essential services.

Technology and development tools

  • Python for data processing, mathematical modelling and optimization.
  • NASA/JPL Horizons API for Sun and Earth ephemeris information.
  • NumPy and SciPy for numerical computation and constrained optimization using the HiGHS solver.
  • Matplotlib for visualization and analysis.
  • A simulated multi-node electrical network for testing energy distribution and storage scenarios.
  • Canva for communicating the project architecture and mission applications.

Creativity and engineering considerations

The creative aspect of LUNACELL GRID is its integration of astronomical geometry with electrical-network optimization. It connects when and where energy may be available with how that energy can be distributed and used to support mission operations.

During development, we considered lunar illumination constraints, communication availability, energy-storage capacity, battery power limits, transmission losses, essential versus flexible electrical loads, and the trade-offs between additional generation and storage infrastructure.

The current prototype establishes the energy-optimization framework using simulated mission scenarios. More detailed integration of high-resolution lunar terrain, local horizon obstructions, and validated site-specific solar generation is part of the continuing development roadmap.
